heading: GPT-2 small’s attention head L10H7 mainly suppresses predicted tokens already present in context
definition: in GPT-2 small, L10H7 mainly suppresses tokens that are both predicted by earlier components and present earlier in the context, across the training distribution.
summary: Independent groups reproduce L10H7’s suppression of previously seen, predicted tokens on constructed prompts in GPT-2 small. The original study provides evidence that this is its main role across the training distribution, but independent groups have not replicated that finding.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B (GPT-2 small): R2 for the suppression role on constructed prompts; R0 for 'mainly ... across the training distribution'. The latter has original evidence from CSPA averaged over OpenWebText and selected behavioural classification, but no independent distribution-wide replication. Other scales do not apply to this version (counts: V1.studies_by_family.GPT-2 = 6; V1.studies_by_size.<1B = 1; V1.studies_by_size.not stated = 5).
suggested_status.reason: Counts: V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 4; V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 0; V1.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0. R2 rests on the different-group constructed-prompt tests: arXiv:2402.11655 finds L10H7 contributes 33% of negative Δcofa and a counterfactual-token logit of -1.13 in unmodified GPT-2 (arXiv:2402.11655#R1, arXiv:2402.11655#R3); arXiv:2508.16109 ablates and inspects GPT-2 small head 10.7 on syllogisms (arXiv:2508.16109#r1, arXiv:2508.16109#r4, arXiv:2508.16109#r5). The qualitative SAE role label is additional evidence, but its author overlap with the original is unestablished and it is not used to establish independence (lw:xmegeW5mqiBsvoaim#r1). The scripted author-overlap count is therefore not used as verified evidence. The original reports 80% three-condition behavioural classification within its top-5% loss-effect sample (arXiv:2310.04625#r1), and separately 76.9% of L10H7's direct KL effect explained by CSPA averaged over OpenWebText (arXiv:2310.04625#r7), alongside weights analyses. These are different measures; the distribution-wide evidence does not rest solely on the selected behavioural sample. Independent repetition of those original measures remains missing (counts: V1.tested_by_tranche.T1 = 1, the original).
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) Would a different group reproduce both the CSPA KL recovery averaged over OpenWebText and the three-condition behavioural classification on an unselected sample? A clear failure would argue for C on the distribution-wide wording. (2) Does L10H7 suppress when only one condition holds (token predicted but absent from context, or present but not predicted)? (3) What happens with a per-head intervention that separates L10H7 from L11H10 in the CounterFact setting? (4) How large is the share of L10H7's harmful completions, which the original reports as almost as many as its helpful ones?

source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: The authors classified OpenWebText completions and compared mean ablation of L10H7, which replaces its output with an average output, with Copy Suppression-Preserving Ablation (CSPA), which preserves its copy-suppression mechanism.
original_result.result: Among the top 5% of completions most affected by mean ablation, 80% met all three copy-suppression conditions. Averaged over OpenWebText, CSPA explained 76.9% of L10H7’s direct effect measured by KL divergence.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: GPT-2 small’s L10H7 suppressed a counterfactual (false) token already in the prompt, boosted by earlier heads.
GPT-2 small’s L10H7 suppressed in-context truth tokens across tested syllogism prompts.
An annotator with limited prior information identified L10H7’s copy-suppression role from sparse autoencoder features.
Boosting GPT-2’s L10H7 and L11H10 together suppressed factually correct tokens already in the prompt.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Whether L10H7's three-condition behavioural classification holds on an unselected OpenWebText sample. In GPT-2 small, the original's 80% classification result concerns the top 5% of completions by loss effect (arXiv:2310.04625#r1). Separately, CSPA recovers 76.9% of L10H7's direct KL effect averaged over OpenWebText, with no top-5% completion restriction stated for that aggregate (arXiv:2310.04625#r7). The missing test is behavioural classification on unselected text.
untested.basis: arXiv:2310.04625#r1, Section 2.1, restricts the behavioural classification to the selected sample; arXiv:2310.04625#r7, Sections 3.3.1–3.3.2, supplies the separate OpenWebText-averaged CSPA result. The untested lines of arXiv:2507.11809, lw:xmegeW5mqiBsvoaim and arXiv:2508.16109 list training-distribution or ordinary-text coverage as missing; counts: versions.V1.studies_with_untested_parts = 5. That count does not establish an absence of all distribution-wide measurements.

untested.what: Another group repeating the original's own method: the three-condition classification of sampled completions, or CSPA. The only T1 test is the original. lw:ebezsHW6qJwxTFasX restates CSPA's 76.9% but is the original's accompanying post and not a test.
untested.basis: counts: V1.tested_by_tranche.T1 = 1 (arXiv:2310.04625's header says T1); V1.tested_by_tranche T2 = 2, T3 = 1, T5 = 1; the lw:ebezsHW6qJwxTFasX header is marked NOT A TEST OF V1.

untested.what: Whether L10H7 needs both conditions, outside the original: no independent study checks that it does not suppress a token that is predicted upstream but absent from context, or present in context but not predicted.
untested.basis: Untested lines of lw:xmegeW5mqiBsvoaim ('Whether suppression is specific to tokens both predicted upstream and present in context') and arXiv:2507.11809 ('whether earlier components predict the token'); no V1 row in the pack contrasts tokens that meet only one condition.

untested.what: An intervention on L10H7 alone in the CounterFact fact/counterfactual setting. Per-head numbers there are logit projections only; the interventions change L10H7 and L11H10 together. (In syllogisms, arXiv:2508.16109 ablates 10.7 alone, r1.)
untested.basis: arXiv:2507.11809 untested line ('isolating L10H7 from L11H10'); arXiv:2402.11655 method-sensitivity line (GPT-2 interventions use L10H7 and L11H10); arXiv:2402.11655's V1 rows R1-R3 are all measurement.

wording_issues.issue: The original's behavioural result (80% of sampled completions meet all three conditions, r1) is on the top 5% of OpenWebText completions by L10H7 mean-ablation effect. The original also reports that this sample accounts for half of L10H7's loss-reducing effect, and that L10H7 is harmful on almost as many completions as it helps (not in rows; Section 2.1, Appendix J.2). The independent supporting results all use constructed prompts (CounterFact-derived in arXiv:2402.11655 and arXiv:2507.11809; templated syllogisms in arXiv:2508.16109) or a qualitative SAE label, and each lists the training distribution as untested.

In GPT-2 small, the original reports that CSPA explains 76.9% of L10H7's direct KL effect averaged over OpenWebText (r7). This measures effect recovery, separately from the 80% behavioural classification within the selected top-5% sample (r1); the percentages have different denominators. arXiv:2508.16109 lists 'mainly' as unquantified relative to other roles, and lw:xmegeW5mqiBsvoaim lists how much of the head's behaviour is copy suppression as untested. arXiv:2402.11655 gives L10H7 33% of the network's negative Δcofa (R1), a share of the network's effect in one task, not of the head's behaviour.

wording_issues.phrase: One head, one role (version name; statement names only L10H7)
wording_issues.issue: In the independent counterfactual and syllogism tests, other heads suppress the same token. arXiv:2402.11655 reports L11H10 at 37% of the negative Δcofa with a counterfactual-token logit of -1.05, the second-lowest of all heads (not in rows, Section 6.3), against L10H7's 33% and -1.13 (R1, R3). arXiv:2507.11809 amplifies L10H7 and L11H10 together and does not resolve results by head (r1, r2 verdict fixes). In arXiv:2508.16109, r5 covers 9.7, 10.7 and 11.10 together.

arXiv:2508.16109's authors call head 10.7's role in syllogisms negation, and its method-sensitivity line says the reported role of 10.7 changes across the Simple, Opposite and Complex formats. The verdict reads the head's own action as suppression of the attended truth token, with the MLP flipping it (r1, r4, r5).

method_sensitivity.factor: Behavioural sample selection, metric and input approximation (original)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2310.04625 reports that its results depend on the behavioural sample chosen (top 5% of completions by L10H7 effect), on KL divergence versus loss-based metrics, and on an idealized versus a more faithful input approximation. Its 80% figure (r1) is from the top-5% sample, and CSPA's 76.9% (r7) is measured with KL divergence.

In GPT-2 with L10H7 and L11H10 amplified together, factual output falls to less than 90% at alpha 5 (r1, rated partial) and to less than 70% at alpha 10 (r2, rated observed). The study reports that the best alpha depends on sentence-structure matching in its robustness experiments, and that head contributions vary by answer category (r6, figure only, not resolved for L10H7).

In GPT-2 small, mean-ablating head 10.7 improves performance beyond baseline in Simple Syllogism (r1), while ablating it by path patching in Opposite Syllogism gives a significant drop in logit difference (r2, cannot_determine: the verdict says this shows 10.7 matters causally, not that it suppresses). The study says 10.7's reported role changes across Simple, Opposite and Complex formats.
